title: Media generation and production
summary: Operational rules for why an image exists, its license, raster format, responsive delivery, SVG trust, and alt text. Each rule links the page for that subject.

rules.title: Purpose before asset
rules.intent: Decide what information or action the image adds before choosing a file
principles: Ask what a person would miss if the image were not there. That answer is the purpose: information, an action, or decoration
If the adjacent text already says it, the image is decorative and should not repeat the text
A hero or illustration with no information and no action does not earn a place in the layout
acceptance: Each asset is marked informative, functional, or decorative, with the reason
limitations: The decision tree tells you how to treat the image after the purpose is known. It does not score whether a decorative image is worth designing

rules.title: Asset provenance
rules.intent: Record who made the image, which license applies, and what that license restricts, before the file ships
principles: Name the creator, the source, and the license for every production image
Use a published license, such as a Creative Commons license, and keep its conditions: attribution, share-alike, noncommercial, or no derivatives
For a generated image, also record the provider and the model. Those terms are the provider's, and they are separate from a Creative Commons license on the file
acceptance: Metadata for each production asset includes origin, creator, license, and, when generated, provider and model
limitations: The Creative Commons license list does not cover a model's terms of use. Those stay on the provider's own terms, which this pack does not restate

rules.title: Raster optimization
rules.intent: Pick a raster format the browser can decode, at the pixel size the layout actually displays
principles: Choose the format for the job: a photographic raster, a transparent raster, or an SVG for a UI glyph that must stay sharp
AVIF and WebP can be smaller than JPEG or PNG. Ship a fallback the browser can decode, because an unsupported encoding is discarded after the download
Export at the displayed size. A multi-megabyte hero that is shown much smaller wastes the transfer
acceptance: The file's pixel dimensions are compared with the displayed size, and a fallback exists for a newer encoding
limitations: Format support moves. The AVIF lesson and the MDN format guide describe the tradeoff. They are not a frozen browser matrix

rules.title: Responsive image delivery
rules.intent: Give the browser a choice of sources, and reserve the aspect ratio so the layout does not jump
principles: Use srcset and sizes when the browser should pick the smallest adequate file. Use picture when you must prescribe the source, such as a different crop or a format fallback
Do not send one large file to every viewport
Set aspect-ratio, or width and height, so the slot matches the image before it loads
antiPatterns: Same large image to all devices
acceptance: A narrow and a wide viewport request different sources when the savings are real, and the slot does not collapse
limitations: aspect-ratio is listed in CSS Snapshot 2026 as safe to release before Candidate Recommendation, in CSS Sizing Level 4. It is not part of the snapshot's official definition

rules.title: SVG security
rules.intent: Use SVG as an image when it is static, and review script before inserting SVG into the document
principles: In an img, background-image, or similar image context, browsers disable SVG script and external resources
Those restrictions do not apply to inline SVG or to SVG embedded with object, embed, or iframe. Script and event handlers there run in the page
Treat an external or user-supplied SVG as untrusted. Review it, or sanitize it, before insertion. An SVG script href that loads an arbitrary URL is an XSS sink
antiPatterns: Raw remote SVG inserted into HTML
acceptance: Static icons are referenced as images. Any inline SVG was reviewed or sanitized
limitations: MDN describes the image-context restrictions as what some browsers do. A sanitizer's allowlist is an implementation choice this page does not specify

rules.title: Informational alt text
rules.intent: Put the image's information in alt when that information is not already in the text nearby
principles: An informative image gets a short alt that carries the meaning, not the file name and not the word image
If the same meaning is already in adjacent text, use an empty alt so it is not read twice
A complex image, such as a chart, puts the data in text on the page. Alt points at that meaning. It does not replace the data
acceptance: The image's meaning is in alt or in the surrounding text, and decorative images use an empty alt
limitations: The informative-images tutorial covers simple images. Charts and groups of images have their own WAI pages, which this rule does not copy
